items.title: One Nation 'spot the Westerner' video condemned
items.description: A One Nation party official who filmed people on Melbourne's streets and claimed the city "doesn't look like a Western nation at all" is condemned by both sides of politics amid the minor party's surge in national opinion polls.

items.title: Parents say daughter's suicidal thoughts were downplayed and dismissed
items.description: A hospital has apologised to the parents of 19-year-old Amber Wraith, who took her own life in 2022. Her family hopes her death will prompt changes in the way mental health patients are treated.

items.title: Gold crashes after 'running on disaster scenario' that is yet to play out
items.description: The precious metals market collapses following the appointment of new US Federal Reserve chair Kevin Warsh, and some analysts say it signals a significant shift in the world's financial markets.

items.title: Ferguson called Epstein 'legend' and said 'just marry me', emails show
items.description: The former Duchess of York's friendship with the late sex offender is back in the spotlight after the latest release of documents about the Epstein case.

items.title: Calls to strip UK politician of title amid Epstein leak claims
items.description: Documents released reportedly show Peter Mandelson sent Jeffrey Epstein briefing notes meant for then-British prime minister Gordon Brown.

items.title: Rate hike calls are near-unanimous, but the dissenters aren't from the fringes
items.description: Could RBA economists conceivably see inflation returning to target without a rate hike? We'll know this afternoon, and while it's not the dominant view, it's not a fringe one either.

items.title: Live: Liberals to sit alone in parliament after Coalition split
items.description: Ahead of parliament's return, the future of the Coalition remains in limbo after "civil" talks between Sussan Ley and David Littleproud. Follow live.

items.title: Brisbane coffee assault enters new phase with justice depending on Beijing
items.description: Sixteen months after a stranger poured scalding coffee over a baby in a Brisbane park, China's decision to send a working group to Australia marks the first tangible shift in a complicated case.

items.title: Deep Creek bushfire burning on 'multiple fast-moving fronts'
items.description: The Country Fire Service is warning that the threat posed by a fire on South Australia's Fleurieu Peninsula could increase throughout the day.

items.title: Boy swims four hours to shore to save family swept out to sea
items.description: A 13-year-old boy has been hailed a hero after swimming four hours through rough seas to get help for his mother and two siblings, who were swept out to sea on an inflatable paddleboard in WA's South West.

items.title: Should you take fish oil for your heart, joints or mood?
items.description: Fish oil is one of the most popular dietary supplements. It's often promoted for protecting the heart, boosting mood, reducing inflammation, and supporting overall health.

items.title: 'Go to the freezer section': Sleeping rough during severe hot weather
items.description: Tim knows firsthand the struggles of being homeless and navigating the weather, but it's experiences like his which will be the focus of a newly formed Australian Climate and Homelessness Alliance.

items.title: Victorian beach community battles global company's offshore turbines
items.description: A tiny coastal community in Victoria's east is battling an international wind energy giant that wants to build 60 to 70 turbines in the ocean 10 kilometres from shore.

items.title: Trial for brain cancer vaccines supported by devastated family of 9yo boy
items.description: The four-year trial of about 70 children with "dismal prognoses" in eight hospitals across Australia will test the safety and effectiveness of the experimental treatment designed to harness the immune system to attack a child's tumour.

items.title: How James Valentine's creative radio style could 'lift the mood of a city'
items.description: Listeners and former colleagues share treasured memories of a veteran broadcaster who has announced his retirement due to cancer.

items.title: 'Incredible' act by critically endangered bat pictured for first time
items.description: Often compared to a "teddy bear", advocates hope the special snap of an endangered flying fox carrying its pup will shine a light on the Christmas Island animal.

items.title: A teacher's debut novel offers a behind-the-scenes look at the classroom
items.description: Sita Walker, an English teacher from Brisbane, explains how she tackled her first work of fiction, set in a single hour at a state high school.

items.title: Blizzards, crevasses and sea ice — the dangers of working in Antarctica
items.description: Antarctica can be a dangerous place to live and work, but to mitigate the risks, a team of survival specialists is contracted to keep Australia's expeditioners safe on the ice.

items.title: More pregnant women drinking in one of Australia's largest regional cities
items.description: A sharp rise in pregnant women drinking alcohol in Australia's largest northern city might be linked to the impact of last year's floods, health authorities say.

items.title: Israel partially reopens Gaza's Rafah crossing to Egypt
items.description: Around 50 Palestinians are expected to cross in each direction on the first day, and no goods will be allowed through.

items.title: Police vow they 'will not stop' until Dezi Freeman is found
items.description: Victoria Police is continuing to search bushland in the Mount Buffalo National Park for traces of alleged gunman Dezi Freeman.

items.title: US and India strike trade deal, slashing tariffs
items.description: The US president says his social media platform that a deal had been struck, which includes a reduction of tariffs on Indian products in exchange for New Delhi no longer buying oil from Russia.

items.title: Two mothers sit inside tennis's top 10 rankings for the first time
items.description: For the first time in women's tennis, two mothers are ranked inside the world's top 10 simultaneously.

items.title: Friends of Boat Harbour beg 'please don't drive on the sand dunes'
items.description: Volunteers have completed phase one of their plan to restore the dunes at a beloved beach in regional WA where 4WDs have destroyed parts of the unique habitat.

items.title: Victorian woman 'heartbroken' after fertility surgery delayed again
items.description: Victorian healthcare workers are continuing strike action for at least another month over pay disputes with the state government, leaving one woman wondering when her fertility surgery will happen.
